There exists a unique family of elements $\Upsilon_{\mu}\in\textbf{U}^{+}_{\mu}$, for $\mu\in{\mathbb{N}}\mathbb{I}$, such that $\Upsilon_{0}=1$ and $\Upsilon=\sum_{\mu\in{\mathbb{N}}\mathbb{I}}\Upsilon_{\mu}$ satisfies the following identity:

(2.1)

$\psi_{\imath}(u)\Upsilon=\Upsilon\psi(u),\qquad\text{for all }u\in{\textbf{U}}^{\imath}.$

Moreover, $\Upsilon_{\mu}=0$ unless ${\mu^{\theta}}=-\mu\in X$. (Recall $\theta=-w_{\bullet}\circ\tau$.)

Quasi K-matrix was originally formulated in order to construct a new bar involution and then $\imath$ canonical bases on based U-modules (see §3 below). On the other hand, a suitable twisting of $\Upsilon$ by elements in $\textbf{U}^{\imath 0}$ provides certain ${\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ -module isomorphisms [8, §2.5] [3] (also see [9, §4.5] for a different formulation), nowadays known as the K-matrix. It is shown in [3] that the K-matrix provides solutions to the reflection equation, an $\imath$ -analog of the Yang-Baxter equation. There has been a reformulation of quasi K-matrix in [1] without referring explicitly to the bar involution of ${\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$; this has the advantage of making sense of quasi K-matrices in general parameters satisfying (1.5)–(1.6).

3. Canonical bases arising from quantum symmetric pairs

3.1. Based modules

The quasi $K$ -matrix $\Upsilon$ in (a completion of) $\textbf{U}^{+}$ induces a $\mathbb{Q}(v)$ -linear map $\Upsilon:M\otimes L(\lambda)\rightarrow M\otimes L(\lambda),$ for any $\lambda\in X^{+}$ and any weight U-module $M$ with weights bounded above. A ${\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ -module $M$ equipped with an anti-linear involution $\psi_{\imath}$ is called $\imath$ -involutive if $\psi_{\imath}(um)=\psi_{\imath}(u)\psi_{\imath}(m),$ for all $u\in{\textbf{U}}^{\imath},m\in M.$ Let $(M,B)$ be a based U-module [55, IV] with weights bounded above. We denote the bar involution on $M$ by $\psi$. Then $M$ is an $\imath$ -involutive ${\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ -module with involution (see [8])

$\psi_{\imath}:=\Upsilon\circ\psi.$

Assume that $(M,B)$ is a based U-module with weights bounded above such that $\Upsilon$ preserves the $\mathcal{A}$ -submodule ${}_{\mathcal{A}}M$. Then the $\mathbb{Q}(v)$ -linear map $\psi_{\imath}=\Upsilon\circ\psi$ (and subsequently, $\Upsilon$ ) preserves the $\mathcal{A}$ -submodule ${}_{\mathcal{A}}M\otimes_{\mathcal{A}}{}_{\mathcal{A}}L(\lambda)$, for any $\lambda\in X^{+}$; see [10]. In particular, the involution $\psi_{\imath}$ on the $\imath$ -involutive ${\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ -module $L(\lambda_{1})\otimes\ldots\otimes L(\lambda_{\ell})$ preserves the $\mathcal{A}$ -submodule ${}_{\mathcal{A}}L(\lambda_{1})\otimes_{\mathcal{A}}\ldots\otimes_{\mathcal{A}}{}_{\mathcal{A}}L(\lambda_{\ell})$, where $\lambda_{i}\in X^{+}$ for $1\leq i\leq\ell$. For $(\textbf{U},{\textbf{U}}^{\imath})$ of finite type, a stronger statement holds [10]: $\Upsilon_{\mu}\in{}_{\mathcal{A}}\textbf{U}^{+}$, for each $\mu$. This generalizes the integrality of quasi R-matrix of finite type due to Lusztig [55, 24.1.6].

Define a partial order $\leq$ on the weight lattice $X$ such that $\lambda\leq\lambda^{\prime}\text{ if and only if }\lambda^{\prime}-\lambda\in{\mathbb{N}}\mathbb{I}.$ For an element $x$ in U or in a U-module $M$ of weight $\mu\in X$, we write $|x|=\mu$.
card.label: Theorem 2.1

paper.title: Quantum symmetric pairs
paper.abstract: This is a survey of some recent progress on quantum symmetric pairs and applications. The topics include quasi K-matrices, $\imath$Schur duality, canonical bases, super Kazhdan-Lusztig theory, $\imath$Hall algebras, current presentations for affine $\imath$quantum groups, and braid group actions.
